subject: Verdant Bio — context footprint & quantization implications for dedicated commit
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@verdantbio.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing ask — 64k experiments + quantization tradeoffs

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We kicked off an internal scoping session and have two immediate asks as we evaluate a Dedicated commitment:

1) Production target is ~30 qps steady-state for our LLM assistant (retrieval-augmented) using a Llama-2-70B variant with 64k context for long-document reasoning.
2) We need a clear mapping from context window / KV cache footprint + quantization choices to GPU sizing (pod count & type) and headroom for spikes.
3) Procurement needs a proposal that shows an initial committed pool and a recommended canary configuration (to validate latency and correctness with our prompt sets).

Attached is an export of representative request sizes and our average response token distribution (verdant_memory_model_profiles.xlsx). Can you put together a short sizing recommendation and a plan for an initial Reserved pool (3-month commit pilot) including expected limitations for 4-bit / 8-bit quantization vs full fp16?

Time is tight — procurement wants something by end of week if possible.

Cheers,
Sara
Sara Lin
Head of AI Systems
Verdant Bio

P.S. Tom from procurement (cc’d) will help with purchase timelines and questions about billing cadence.
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@verdantbio.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@procureco.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — 64k experiments + quantization tradeoffs

Sara / Tom —

Thanks — we can get a concise sizing plan together today and a short technical appendix that explains the memory math. High-level answer up front:

- Baseline (fp16) for Llama-2-70B @ 64k will require roughly ~120–140GB GPU memory per concurrent model replica if we keep a full KV in-GPU and allow for 2x activation/headroom. That maps to H100/A100-80GB class hardware with KV offload or multiple-GPU partitioning.
- With 8-bit quantization (int8/q8 variants) you generally reduce model weights by ~2x — realistic per-rep GPU requirement drops to ~60–80GB, which lets you fit a single replica on an 80GB GPU with tighter headroom.
- Aggressive 4-bit quantization (gptq/q4* styles) can reduce weight storage 3–4x; combined with KV compression and prefix caching we can often fit a production replica into a 48–64GB device for lighter loads, but this increases evaluation risk (deterministic regressions) and requires a prompt-specific eval suite.

I’ll circulate a short table with pod counts and recommended reserved pool sizes plus a minimal canary config. We’ll also call out latency expectations for the three quant tiers.

Attaching a one-pager and asking Marcus and Karthik to validate numbers (cc’d).

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@verdantbio.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@procureco.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Verdant Bio — draft sizing calc and pod recommendations

Marcus / Karthik —

Following Sara’s ask, draft below (numbers rounded and include conservative headroom). Please confirm or correct and add notes about KV offload and batching assumptions.

Summary assumptions (from Verdant profile):
- Target steady qps: 30 qps (concurrent request distribution ~12 long sessions, 18 short).
- Avg prompt + response tokens per request: 1,800 tokens (heavy retrieval + summarization).
- Model: Llama-2-70B with 64k context (static KV kept during request; dynamic KV for session history).
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 800 ms for short requests, p95 <= 1.6s for long requests.

Memory math (high-level):
- Model weights (fp16): ~140 GB resident.
- KV cache memory = sequence_length * hidden_size * 2 (key+value) * 4 bytes (fp32)/2 bytes (fp16) — for 64k sequence we estimate KV ~40–50GB depending on hidden_size and packing.
- Activations + working memory + batch buffers: ~10–20GB depending on concurrency and batching strategy.
- Conservative per-rep footprint (fp16, full KV on-GPU): 140 + 45 + 15 = ~200GB (this forces multi-GPU sharded replica).

Quantization impact (rough expected reductions):
- int8 / q8: weights ~2x reduction -> weights ~70 GB. KV remains same if stored as fp16/fp32 (we typically compress KV to fp16). So per-rep becomes ~70 + 45 + 15 = ~130GB -> fit on 2x 80GB GPUs with modest headroom (or single 160GB-class partition).
- q4 / 4-bit: weights ~3.5x reduction -> weights ~40 GB. Combined footprint ~40 + 45 + 15 = ~100GB -> fits on a single 80GB GPU if KV offload or on a 64–80GB device if KV compressed/offloaded.

Pod & fleet recommendations (initial pilot):
Option A — Conservative (fp16, multi-GPU replicas):
- Replica shape: 1 logical replica = 2x H100-80GB (model sharded + KV on-GPU)
- Desired headroom: 20% for spikes -> plan for 6 logical replicas to support 30 qps steady (target concurrency + autoscale buffer)
- Reserved pool: 12x H100-80GB GPUs (maps to 6 replicas). Canary: 1 replica (2 GPUs).

Option B — Balanced (int8 / q8):
- Replica shape: 1 logical replica = 1x H100-80GB (weights quantized to int8, KV in fp16)
- Reserved pool: 8x H100-80GB (estimate supports 30 qps with autoscaling buffers)
- Canary: 2 replicas (2 GPUs total).

Option C — Aggressive (q4 + KV offload):
- Replica shape: 1 logical replica = 1x 64–80GB GPU (q4 weights + KV offloaded to host or NVMe with caching)
- Additional engineering: KV offload + prefix cache and batch tuning
- Reserved pool: 6x 80GB-class GPUs (lower cost but higher ops risk)
- Canary: 2 replicas + KV offload validation.

Operational notes:
- We recommend the customer sign up for a roll-out window where we run canary tests with their eval suite (we will run full prompt regression to detect quality regressions when using q4).
- For procurement the safe option is Option B — it buys a 1x GPU-per-rep topology and materially reduces committed GPU count vs Option A while keeping lower risk than Option C.
- Include a 3-month commit pilot with a clause to switch quantization profiles after successful QA.

Next steps: Marcus, can you produce a quick cost delta estimate (monthly committed GPU cost) for Options A/B/C? Karthik, can you prepare a short runbook for KV offload and canary validation steps? I’ll package this for Sara and procurement.

Thanks —
Stephanie
